SUBJECT: ONE ONE-HANDED CUTLASS called the FEN CUTLASS, a sturdy marsh-raider's chopping sword. POINT UP, pommel down, the hilt upright on the vertical centre line of the picture, seen from the side. From the bottom: a small rounded brass POMMEL CAP; a GRIP for ONE fist, ribbed, wound with bright silver wire, slightly swelling in the middle; a BRASS HAND GUARD: a broad brass KNUCKLE-BOW that sweeps from the pommel cap down to the guard in a smooth loop on the RIGHT side of the grip, joined by two or three thinner brass side bars that curve around it like a cage, with a short brass quillon sticking out on the LEFT where it meets the blade, and a flat brass shell at the base of the blade; then the BLADE: SHORT and BROAD, single-edged, its cutting edge on the RIGHT, gently CURVED so it leans a little to the right as it rises, of even breadth most of the way, ending in a CLIPPED point: the straight back on the LEFT angles sharply in near the top to meet the curved edge in a point. Dark, slightly weathered steel with a soft lighter edge, and a faint darker etched leaf-and-scroll pattern near the hilt, kept very simple. The blade is about three times as long as the grip. Colours: warm polished brass, silver wire, darkish weathered steel.
